PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add connection diagnostics for remote hosts
PullRequest.Body:
## What changes

Make remote-host state inspectable from the Agents UI, including on a phone and when the host picker is empty. **Show Connection Diagnostics** opens a compact sheet with Copy, Download, Refresh, and Close actions.

The report presents factual, collapsible sections:

- Tunnel discovery outcome and count
- Each host's connection state and picker availability
- Recent activity, oldest first
- Client information, collapsed at the bottom and included in exports

For example, a successful discovery can find a host that is absent from the picker because it was persistently dismissed. The report exposes the discovery result, dismissal flag, cache state, and picker membership together rather than leaving the user with only "No Host."

Copy and Download export the displayed snapshot, including collapsed content, without requiring a live remote. Refresh reads local state; it does not initiate discovery or reconnect. History is bounded to the current window, and the report does not infer root causes.

## Implementation

- Keep the diagnostics model, service, report, commands, and tests together in the remote-host contribution.
- Record background and interactive discovery through one wrapper that preserves results and errors.
- Read persisted dismissal/suppression through the tunnel service's API.
- Extend the shared mobile sheet with opt-in non-dismissing header actions and focus containment; retain existing caller defaults.
- Provide accessibility help, a plain-text Accessible View, and a verbosity setting.

## Manual validation

- Windows desktop Agents: real clipboard and Electron download, a configured WebSocket mock, controlled disconnect/recovery, and accessibility-help/Accessible View round trips.
- Regular desktop VS Code: startup, untitled editor and terminal opening, and absence of the Agents-only diagnostics command.
- Authenticated web Agents in Chromium phone emulation: populated and empty host pickers, persisted dismissal and explicit restoration, interactive discovery history, actual copy/download contents, and 393px layout.
- Full-sheet fixtures at phone and desktop widths.

Real iOS/Android devices, production Dev Tunnels/SSH/WSL/Dev Container connections, screen-reader speech, and auxiliary-window acceptance remain outstanding. Hardware Back integration is deferred.

## Branch relationship

This is a **stacked PR**, based on `aamunger/remoteConnections` to keep the separately reviewed cache-preservation changes out of this PR's diff. It should not be merged into that feature branch accidentally; retarget to `main` after the base work lands, or rebase/split as appropriate.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path and complexity are direct: every successful tracked discovery executes this filter before resolving, and TunnelAgentHostStorage.isTunnelDismissed performs Array.includes over a persisted list. The only uncertainty is how often users accumulate enough dismissed IDs and returned tunnels for the delay to become conspicuous, so severity is low rather than omitting the proven mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU string comparisons over the persisted dismissed-tunnel array.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added cost grows as discovered tunnel count multiplied by persisted dismissed-ID count, rather than linearly with the discovery result.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous completion latency and UI-thread CPU after each successful tunnel enumeration.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same enumeration returned its tunnel array to the caller without an additional diagnostics-wide dismissal count; the network request count and existing reconciliation remained unchanged.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successful startup, focus-triggered, rediscover, interactive, or post-delete enumeration now counts dismissed results synchronously before trackDiscovery resolves.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 111 filters every discovered tunnel and calls isTunnelDismissed; before this PR, listTunnels resolved directly to its existing callers without this diagnostics counting pass.
Findings.Title: Build a set before counting dismissed tunnels
Findings.Impact: Accounts with many tunnels and a long-lived set of dismissed tunnel IDs can pause after enumeration completes before startup host status, the host picker, or rediscovery becomes ready.
Findings.Evidence: trackDiscovery line 111 invokes isTunnelDismissed once per returned tunnel. TunnelAgentHostStorage.isTunnelDismissed uses `_dismissedTunnels.get().includes(tunnelId)`, while dismissTunnel appends unique IDs to the application-scoped persisted array and IDs are removed only by an explicit clear. Therefore a result of T tunnels with D historical dismissals adds O(T*D) string comparisons on the discovery completion path.
Findings.Recommendation: Read getTunnelVisibility once, construct a Set from `dismissed`, and count with Set.has (or expose set-backed membership) so the added diagnostics pass is O(T + D) while preserving the same count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup, focus-triggered, and manual background tunnel discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TunnelAgentHostContribution calls `_silentStatusCheck`, which awaits `trackDiscovery`, which awaits `listTunnels`; diagnostics copying/counting must finish before cache reconciliation, connection-status updates, and host-picker readiness proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate dev tunnels through `ITunnelAgentHostService.listTunnels({ silent: true })`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network enumeration per existing status-check invocation; no additional network call from diagnostics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same status-check triggers made one network enumeration, but returned results were not passed through the additional diagnostics counting pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before host cache/status reconciliation; the new local O(T*D) count also completes before the await resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T returned tunnels and D application-persisted dismissed tunnel IDs; the new dismissed count performs T lookups over the D-element array.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each invocation awaits one enumeration, but `_silentStatusCheck` itself has no new coalescing and pre-existing startup/focus/status triggers may overlap. This PR does not increase network concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The network enumeration behavior is unchanged. Diagnostics replaces its last-successful tunnel snapshot on success and retains it for the window; dismissed IDs come from persistent application storage and are not capped.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added per-tunnel call and array-backed membership implementation directly establish O(T*D) synchronous work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical tunnel and dismissal counts are unknown; the persisted dismissal list has no cap, so only prevalence and milliseconds are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated-work regression because the diff adds quadratic local work to every successful discovery completion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Connect via Dev Tunnel and refresh after deletion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication/session lookup precedes the picker; the picker then awaits one tracked tunnel enumeration. A confirmed deletion awaits deletion and then a second, sequential enumeration before the picker is updated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate tunnels for the interactive picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call when opening the flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One direct listTunnels call populated the picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks picker population; diagnostics adds local processing before results return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete a selected tunnel, then enumerate tunnels again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delete and one refresh only after a user confirms deletion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same delete and refresh boundaries existed; only the refresh result is newly tracked.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T returned tunnels and D persisted dismissed IDs for each successful enumeration; picker sorting remains O(T log T).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial enumeration is singular. Delete and post-delete refresh are sequential; diagnostics adds no new concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The interactive path reads fresh tunnel inventory rather than the diagnostics snapshot. Diagnostics only replaces its last-successful in-memory inventory and bounded activity records.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged boundary cardinality and the added local scan; no additional network fan-out was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large enterprise/account inventories are possible but their distribution is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported dismissal-scan finding; no separate boundary-fanout issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, refresh, copy, download, and Accessible View for connection diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Open/refresh synchronously snapshots local configuration, cached/configured/connected/discovered/visible hosts, builds text, and creates report DOM. Copy awaits one clipboard write; download performs one local UTF-8 buffer conversion and browser download trigger. Accessible View reuses the captured text.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build plain-text diagnostics and, on download, encode it into a byte buffer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One text construction per open/refresh; one byte-buffer conversion per download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No diagnostics snapshot, report DOM, clipboard export, or download existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot and DOM construction block opening/refresh; encoding occurs synchronously on the click path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the displayed snapshot to the clipboard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per accepted Copy action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only for feedback and button re-enable; it does not block remote connection workflows.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H distinct host addresses, up to 100 activity events, and report text bytes. Persisted hidden IDs contribute to H even when absent from current discovery/cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Open is guarded by a single active report. Each header action is individually suppressed while pending, though different actions can run independently; no remote work is launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Opening creates a fresh local snapshot unless one is supplied by Accessible View. Refresh replaces it; copy/download reuse the displayed snapshot. Last discovery is retained in memory for the window, and activity is capped at 100.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that all snapshot/render/export work is local and scales with H/text size; low confidence that the linear eager DOM/text costs alone cross a user-visible threshold.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host inventories are usually expected to be modest; no evidence establishes enough report nodes or bytes for hidden-section rendering or export allocation alone to be independently reportable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: no network probe is introduced, history is bounded, actions reuse the snapshot, and linear report rendering/export lacks evidence of harmful magnitude.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connection state and browser lifecycle activity recording
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Remote connection-change events synchronously scan current connections, deduplicate state strings, and append activity before event dispatch returns. Browser online/offline/visibility and configuration changes append one record.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: C current connections per connection-change event; retained activity is capped at 100 and connection-state keys are removed when connections disappear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event handling on the renderer thread; no queues, subprocesses, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A map deduplicates unchanged connection states. Activity drops the oldest entry beyond 100; all state is window-lifetime only.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that cleanup and deduplication prevent unbounded retention and duplicate history.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Connection counts and event rates are not measured, but both are naturally limited and retained history is explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: O(C) event processing and capped state are proportionate to the small connection inventory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Shared mobile content-sheet header actions and focus containment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening creates a fixed number of header controls and hover delegates; Tab handling rebuilds an array from header and registered body focus targets. Closing disposes listeners immediately and removes the overlay after the existing animation delay.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Four diagnostics header controls plus one report target per collapsed section; cost occurs only while the sheet is open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A pending flag coalesces repeated activation of the same async header action. Separate controls are independent; no expensive remote boundary is reachable from Refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. Body focus targets are replaced on refresh, and all references/listeners are disposed on close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that lifecycle cleanup is complete and no boundary fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of sections follows host count, but ordinary Tab events and fixed controls do not establish significant cost for realistic inventories.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: focus handling and hover creation are bounded to the open sheet and disposed correctly.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 28 changed files. One low-severity repeated-work regression was submitted: a new per-result linear dismissal lookup makes successful discovery completion O(T*D). Network call cardinality is unchanged; diagnostics history and lifecycle state are bounded, and no other changed rendering, serialization, cleanup, concurrency, or boundary behavior met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
